title: ATO reminds crypto holders: you still need to declare it — even if the exchange is offshore
excerpt: The Tax Office has flagged crypto as a focus area this year, with new data-matching reaching 1.4 million accounts. If you held, traded, or earned crypto in FY 2025-26, you need to declare it.
body:
The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) has reminded Australians that crypto-asset transactions — including holding, trading, staking, airdrops, and using crypto to buy goods or services — are taxable events and must be declared in this year's tax return.

The reminder comes as the ATO expands its data-matching program to cover more than 1.4 million crypto accounts reported by Australian and offshore exchanges under the global Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), which came into effect on 1 July 2025.

Assistant Commissioner Tim Loh said the ATO is now seeing "a complete picture" of crypto activity for most Australian holders and "the gap between what people report and what we can see has closed significantly".
whatItMeans: If you held crypto at any point in FY 2025-26: Even a no-trade holding creates a CGT event when you eventually sell, swap, or use it. Keep records of the cost base (what you paid in AUD) and the date you acquired it.

If you traded: Every disposal (sell, swap, use to buy something) is a CGT event. You need a record of the value in AUD at the time of the transaction. Use a tool like Koinly, CoinTracker, or the ATO's own record-keeping templates.
If you earned staking rewards or airdrops: These are ordinary income at the AUD value when received. Even if you did not sell, you owe tax on the value in the year received.
If your exchange is offshore: The ATO has the data anyway under CARF. Failing to declare is the worst possible outcome — penalties are typically 75% of the tax avoided, plus interest.
